questions.prompt: Can a super PAC give $10,000 directly to a House candidate's campaign?
questions.why: Super PACs can raise unlimited money but can't give to candidates or coordinate with them. They can only spend independently.

questions.prompt: KENTUCKIANS NOT CORRUPTION (a super PAC) has spent $1.0M in KY's 6th District House race. Which party is it helping?
questions.why: Its spending supports the Democrat or attacks their opponent. Every group's filings list who it backs or opposes.

questions.prompt: Groups helping Democrats have spent $374K in MI's 1st District House race. Are Democrats playing offense or defense?
questions.why: Republicans hold this seat now, so money helping Democrats here is offense.

questions.prompt: In MI's 10th District House race, outside money favors Republicans by $3.5M. Whose nominee has raised more?
questions.why: Outside money and candidate money point opposite ways here: the Democrat leads fundraising by $1.6M.

A party's coordinated spending in the last three weeks before Nov. 3 is disclosed when?
questions.why: Coordinated spending appears only on regular reports. Anything after Oct. 14 lands on the post-general report, due Dec. 3.

questions.prompt: What starts the clock on a 24- or 48-hour spending report?
questions.why: The reporting clock starts on the dissemination date, when the ad first reaches the public.
